definitions.explanation: A door that opens by sliding sideways along a groove or rail rather than swinging on hinges. Common in traditional Japanese architecture (shoji, fusuma) and also widely used in modern Japanese homes for closets, entryways, and room partitions.

examples.japanese: この{部屋|へや}の{入|い}り{口|ぐち}は{引|ひ}き{戸|ど}になっている。
examples.english: The entrance to this room is a sliding door.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}は{開閉|かいへい}に{場所|ばしょ}を{取|と}らないので、{狭|せま}い{部屋|へや}に{向|む}いている。
examples.english: Since sliding doors don't take up space when they open and close, they suit small rooms.

notes:
Compound of {引|ひ}く (to pull) + {戸|と} (door). Contrasted with hinged doors, which require swing-out clearance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}を{開|あ}ける: to open a sliding door
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}を{閉|し}める: to close a sliding door
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}の{部屋|へや}: a room with sliding doors

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {開|ひら}き{戸|ど}: hinged door — opens by swinging on hinges
- {襖|ふすま}: fusuma — paper-and-wood sliding panel for interior partitions
- {障子|しょうじ}: shoji — sliding screen of translucent paper on a wooden frame
